messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — high tail latency affecting tenant=hydra on dedicated-pool=aurora-vpc. symptom=95th token latency > 2.5s, error-rate spike 3%. Page sent to #eng-oncall and #support 3687654321
maya: picking this up. oncall maya. looking at dashboard now — can someone grab scheduler logs for hydra?
taylor: i have logs streaming. seeing large batches stuck in queue around worker-7. likely max_batch_tokens overshoot for hydra's workload. sample log: `worker=7 queue_len=184 max_batch_tokens=2048 avg_seq=256`
sam: confirmed. hydra's request pattern has a lot of short prompts but occasional very long ones, kernel is waiting to fill batch. causing head-of-line blocking.
maya: action plan: 1) lower hydra max_batch_tokens to 512 as a quick mitigation 2) apply bespoke queue-shaper to prefer small requests for x minutes 3) monitor tail latency and errors 4) if no improvement rollback knobs. assigning taylor to step 1 and noah to step 2. ira to notify customer.
ira: on it — i'll message the hydra account ops channel and give ETA ~10m for mitigation. will mention potential limited throughput during tweak.
noah: prepping queue-shaper config. proposed transient config: `queue_shaper: { tenant: \"hydra\", mode: \"small-first\", window_ms: 120000 }`
taylor: applying immediate knob change now. running admin script:```\ncurl -X POST \"https://infra-api.internal/admin/scheduler/knob\" \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{"tenant":"hydra","knob":"max_batch_tokens","value":512,"reason":"oncall mitigation - tail latency"}'\n```deploy-bot: config apply queued on conductor. change id=chg-20260315-8901\ndeploy-bot: change chg-20260315-8901 applied to pool aurora-vpc (propagated to workers in ~12s)
taylor: change is live. i've verified worker-7 now shows `max_batch_tokens=512`. watching metrics.
maya: noah — go ahead with queue-shaper once we see baseline drop start, coordinate timeout to 5m.
noah: applying shaper now: `kubectl apply -f /ops/shapers/hydra-small-first.yaml` -> applied. shaper pod started.
ops-bot: EVENT: metric update at +30s: hydra 95th latency dropped from 2.6s -> 1.1s, error-rate down to baseline 0.2%.
sam: nice. tail latency still has a few spikes around long sequences but overall improved. suggests knobs helped for small-prompt majority.
ira: emailed hydra-ops: "we observed tail latency and applied temporary scheduler knobs and queue shaper; we expect significant improvement; will follow up with postmortem and permanent profile suggestions"
maya: great. next steps: 1) run simulated load to validate throughput impact 2) prepare a permanent per-tenant profile (quantization/batch sizing) 3) create an after-action note and tag product for potential SLA discussion. taylor, sam — can you own sim and perf delta?
taylor: yes — running load test now against canary credentials. prelim result: throughput dip ~8% for small prompts, p95 latency stable. posting results in 10m.
sam: i'll start drafting postmortem skeleton. include timeline, root cause (batch fill waiting due to huge max_batch_tokens for mixed short/long workload), and recommended fixes (adaptive max_batch_tokens, shaper as safety valve).
maya: handing off monitoring to night oncall noah at 3687654900. I'll update the incident channel and mark this thread as follow-up required. thanks all. :thumbsup:
noah: ack. will keep an eye and escalate if spikes return.
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) — hydra tail-latency improved to target thresholds. follow-up ticket created: INFRA-4721 (owner: sam)
